The motor is connected to front axle through a single gear ratio: in these vehicles there’s usually no need for a
transmission (the motor is meant as a P4).
The new 500e is an example of BEV: it is equipped with a 70 kW/95 Cv motor, supplied by 400 V battery. The

slides.body:
BEV
The left schematic is taken from a
Stellantis program and shows the
main powertrain controllers used on
T
he BEV:
BPCM: HV battery pack controller
estimates battery voltage, power
limits and commands contactors,
battery heating and cooling
components
IDCM: this module is usually divided
in two subsystems: OBCM and APM.
OBCM is responsible for interfacing
with external charger (EVSE) for HV
battery; The APM controls the DC/DC
converter for LV battery charging.

slides.title: BEV Architecture & Torque Control
slides.body:
BEV
EVCU: is the main powertrain
system controller; based on
vehicle status and driver action, it
generates inputs for the other
modules and also computes the
torque demands for the motor.
This module also contain the
standard vehicle functions as
Cruise Control, Speed limiter,
One Pedal Drive etc.
EDM: this module is responsible
for translating the torque
demand from EVCU into
electrical inputs (phase currents
and voltage) to drive the motor.

slides.title: BEV Architecture & Torque Control Overview REEV
slides.body:
BEV
The electrical vehicles can use the motor to generate both positive and negative power. In this latter
case, the motor is used as a generator to recharge the HV battery and thus to increase vehicle
autonomy.
Find below some scenarios in which the motor can exploit some external energy source to
regenerate the battery:
- Regenerative braking (One Pedal Drive): the electrical motor is used to brake the vehicle,
converting the kinetic energy of the car into electrical energy for battery charging. When OPD is
active the vehicle can be driven without using brake pedal: the motor generates a positive torque
when pedal percentage is above the neutral point and a negative braking torque when the
percentage is below the neutral position, thus the driver can perform almost any kind of
maneuver by properly tuning the accelerator pedal position.
- Cruise Control or Speed Limiter holding the vehicle on a negative grade: on the BEV, CC
and SL can hold the speed target even on high negative grades, thanks to the braking capability
of the electrical motor. In this scenario the potential energy of the grade is converted and used to
recharge the battery

slides.title: Overview MHEV vehicles
slides.body:
The REEV (range extended electric vehicle) is a particular kind of hybrid, in which the Internal Combustion Engine
(ICE) is only used for recharging the HV battery and thus to increase the vehicle expected range.
We can thus say that in the REEV, only series hybrid mode is available.
The typical REEV architecture consists of an electrical motor (a P4 as on standard BEV), meant for demanded
torque actuation and an ICE, connected to a secondary electrical motor (a P0 or a P1). The latter works as a
generator and uses the torque produced by the ICE to recharge the battery.
